newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptians offer shares in new steel firm.
newsitem.headline: Egyptians offer shares in new steel firm.

text.p: The founders of a new Egyptian steel firm on Thursday offered the public 360,000 shares or 30 percent of its equity at 100 pounds ($29.40) each.
The founders -- two state-owned banks, six firms and an individual -- said in an advertisement they already held 840,000 shares of the 1.2 million issued shares of Suez Steel.
The firm, to be set up in the Red Sea province of Suez, will produce steel billets, they added.
The forecast return on capital would not be less than 20 percent a year, said the advertisement.

Applications should be for not less than five shares, and only a quarter of the nominal value would be paid, the founders said. The firm will ask for the rest within five years from the date of establishment.
The public offer will continue for 15 days from February 11, with the National Bank of Egypt acting as agent.
